T01.rationale: The same team built Velodrome, the largest DEX on Optimism, and Aerodrome, the largest DEX on Base, both still running. Outcomes are verifiable; individual founders' earlier careers are not documented in sources found.

T03.rationale: Named CEO (Cutler), CFO (Wick) and foundation executive director, plus several engineers visible in git history; no documented succession, and public code activity rests on 3 contributors over 90 days.

T04.rationale: In-house team wrote and maintains the ve(3,3) v2 design (managed veNFTs, Aero Fed emissions), Slipstream and dynamic-fee modules, with public specs; most core math is adapted from Solidly and Uniswap V3.

T05.rationale: No enforcement, lawsuit or misconduct allegation found in press coverage; court records and team wallet histories were not checked, so not a 4.

notes: team_vesting_months NOT set. One source says the team cliff is Feb 2028 (AERO-08), another that the 8.61% foundation+team allocation vests 'over time' (AERO-07); the lock was not verified on-chain, and the team also receives up to 5% of weekly emissions.

T07.rationale: veAERO holders vote weekly and bindingly on emissions allocation and the tail rate, but the team multisig still holds pauser, fee-manager, factory-registry and vetoer roles; the vetoer renunciation is promised without a date.

notes: missing: foundation/team treasury addresses and any periodic treasury or buyback report to reconcile against on-chain balances

T09.rationale: No private sale or VC allocation at genesis; one source names Coinbase Ventures (via the Base Ecosystem Fund) as an investor, with terms undisclosed.

P01.rationale: Traders pay real fees (~$57M annualised in July 2026, >$17B 30d volume), but the liquidity side is paid for with AERO emissions.

P02.rationale: Mainnet since August 2023 (~35 months) with Slipstream concentrated liquidity live since April 2024.

P03.rationale: Fork of Velodrome V2 (Solidly lineage) and adapted Uniswap V3 pools, with meaningful additions: managed veNFTs, gauge-integrated CL pools, dynamic fee modules.

P04.rationale: Uses battle-tested constant-product and concentrated-liquidity designs; no contract exploit in ~3 years of production.

P05.rationale: Single-chain dependence on Base and its sequencer for the core business, and a centralised web domain that was hijacked twice (2023, 2025).

notes: github_commits_90d counts only public repos reachable here; Aero merger work appears to be private, so the low count understates engineering activity.

P08.rationale: Slipstream and dynamic fees shipped, but the flagship Aero merger targeted for Q2 2026 was not live by 1 July 2026, and Predictive Allocation was still 'scheduled'.

P09.rationale: Contracts are public (GPL/Apache, gauges BUSL); the reviewer could not confirm deployed bytecode matches a tagged commit.

P10.rationale: Repos ship a specification, an exhaustive admin-permissions list and a voting-escrow spec; no threat model found.

notes: missing: finding-by-finding remediation status in the Spearbit (2023) and ChainSecurity (2025) reports, and confirmation that Base deployments match the audited commits

contracts_verified NOT set. The project README links every core address to Basescan '#code' (AERO-02), but that is the project's own claim; Basescan, Blockscout and Sourcify were blocked here, so verification was not independently confirmed. Two-minute analyst check: open the Basescan links for AERO 0x9401…8631, Minter, Voter, VotingEscrow, PoolFactory and the Slipstream CLFactory.

S05.rationale: Admin powers sit with a team multisig and an Emergency Council multisig, not an EOA; threshold and signer independence unknown; powers include pausing v1 swaps and swapping fee modules with no timelock.

S06.rationale: Only the Minter contract can mint, on a coded schedule that veAERO voters can nudge by 1 bp of supply per week; no freeze or blacklist function. Supply is uncapped.

S08.rationale: Contracts never exploited, but users lost ~$700K (Nov 2025) and >$40K (Nov 2023) to two DNS hijacks of the official front end; compensation grants were announced but no payout found.
notes: unreimbursed_exploit_usd is set to 0 because no smart-contract exploit was found. Users lost ~$700K (Nov 2025) and >$40-100K (Nov 2023) through DNS hijacks of the official front end; the foundations promised proportional grants (AERO-16/17) and no payout was found before 17 Jul 2026. If the venue counts official-front-end phishing losses as 'users owed money', RF04 would fire. Ask the team for proof the grants were paid.

S09.rationale: Swaps do not depend on an external price oracle; risk sits with third parties that read Aerodrome pool prices, not with the DEX's own solvency.

S10.rationale: AERO is minted natively on Base; the planned Aero expansion to Ethereum and Arc would add cross-chain exposure that is not yet live.

K01.rationale: Locked AERO (veAERO) receives 100% of trading fees plus bribes from the pools it votes for, live since 2023.

notes: top10_holder_pct_ex_contracts NOT set: most supply sits in the VotingEscrow contract as veNFTs, so concentration needs veNFT-owner-level data; explorers were not reachable.
price_to_last_round_multiple NOT set: no priced private round disclosed (Coinbase Ventures/Base Ecosystem Fund terms unknown).

K09.rationale: Minting is on-chain and formulaic, but providers disagree on circulating supply (~958M vs ~1.25B) and the team lock was not verified on-chain.

K10.rationale: The 10% airdrop went out as locked veAERO (AirdropDistributor creates locked NFTs), so recipients could not dump on day one; post-unlock retention not measured.

notes: daa_90d_change_pct NOT set: the only figure is Q1-2026 vs Q4-2025 (-34%), which is stale; May fees +40% vs March suggest activity recovered.
retention_30d_pct NOT set: needs own cohort query.

incentivised_tvl_share_pct NOT set. Structurally, staked LPs give up fees for AERO emissions, so most TVL is likely in emission-receiving gauges; RF15 (mercenary TVL) may well apply. Needs a gauge-staked TVL / total TVL query.
missing: address clustering / funding-source analysis of Aerodrome traders and LPs
live_integrations_count NOT set: no dated list of live integrations found.

O09.rationale: Third-party protocols pay bribes to veAERO voters to direct liquidity (~22% of Q1-2026 value flow) and 180+ tokens are listed; activity depends on that incentive market.

notes: depth_2pct_usd, spread_bps, volume_24h_usd and top_venue_volume_share_pct NOT set: only current venue data is available, which would leak post-listing information.
missing: point-in-time CEX order-book depth and volume by venue for mid-July 2026

M06.rationale: Pre-listing venues evidenced: Coinone (since 2024), KuCoin and Aerodrome itself; other tier-1 venues not confirmed from pre-listing sources.

notes: missing: AERO perp open interest and funding history before 17 July 2026
realized_vol_30d_pct NOT set: no pre-listing daily price series retrievable (CoinGecko API blocked).
missing: ownership of AERO/USDC and AERO/WETH LP positions on Aerodrome (POL vs gauge-staked third parties)

M10.rationale: Leader of Base DEX trading, but Base DEX volume was ~50% below its Oct 2025 peak and AERO ~87% below its high; the merger is a pending catalyst.

B02.rationale: Revenue comes from swaps across many pools but is cyclical (Q1-2026 fees -37% q/q, May +40% vs March), and ~22% is bribes paid by protocols.

B03.rationale: All fees and bribes are distributed weekly on-chain to veAERO voters; cumulative >$295M by Jan 2026.

notes: incentives_to_revenue NOT set. Rough range only: ~11-18% annual inflation on ~1.87B supply at ~$0.45 is ~$90-150M/yr of emissions against ~$57-89M annualised revenue, i.e. ~1-2.5x. Too derived to enter as a metric.
runway_months NOT set: foundation/Dromos treasury not published.
revenue_qoq_growth_pct NOT set: Q1-2026 was -37% q/q; Q2-2026 total not retrievable.
missing: fee share by pool and by top LP/trader addresses

B10.rationale: Staked LPs give their fees to voters and are paid in emissions, so liquidity would thin if emissions stopped; a fee-paying swap business would remain.

C01.rationale: Spot DEX trading is a large segment ($613B in Oct 2025), but Base DEX volume had fallen ~50% from its Oct 2025 peak.

C03.rationale: Base DEX share fell from 72% (Q4-2024) to a ~39% trough before recovering to 43-53% in May 2026; the sources disagree on the latest level.

C04.rationale: Bribe/emission marketplace and Base-native liquidity give a moat, but Uniswap took share to ~32% while Aerodrome fell from 72% to ~43%.

C05.rationale: Code is forkable (Aerodrome is itself a fork; gauges are BUSL-licensed), but liquidity depth and the bribe market are sticky; no fork that took share was found.

C06.rationale: Versus Uniswap, projects can buy liquidity through bribes rather than seed it themselves; one axis, and other ve(3,3) DEXs can copy it.

C07.rationale: Q1-2026 price/sales ~2.2x circulating vs Uniswap 2.3x; on FDV 4.6x vs 3.3x — roughly in line.

C08.rationale: Base was 'exploring' a native token (Sep 2025) and Uniswap competes on the same chain; no competing native DEX from Coinbase/Base found.

notes: missing: list of announced partnerships to test against on-chain flows

C10.rationale: Adds the leading Base DEX token, but the venue already covers DEX tokens; Base is a rival exchange's chain.

notes: missing: social engagement analytics (X, Discord, Telegram) for H1 2026
holders_count NOT set: no pre-listing indexer snapshot retrievable.
missing: disclosed or detected paid-promotion campaigns
missing: grant programme and external contributor data
governance_participation_pct NOT set: weekly gauge voting is near-universal among veAERO holders, but ProtocolGovernor/EpochGovernor participation data was not retrievable.

D08.rationale: Both DNS incidents were flagged publicly within hours with a preliminary root cause in days; a Velodrome post was deleted and the compensation programme had no public follow-up in sources found.

D09.rationale: AERO fell 19% on the merger announcement and sat ~87% below its high; informed opinion appears mixed.

D10.rationale: Largest DEX on Base, integrated with major wallets' security tooling and reportedly backed via Coinbase's Base Ecosystem Fund.

L01.rationale: Aerodrome Foundation and Dromos Labs are named with executives, but an exchange disclosure lists the foundation's jurisdiction and legal form as unknown.

L02.rationale: Lockers receive 100% of fees, a profit-like feature, and the team keeps admin roles; but there was no token sale, and emissions governance is on-chain.

notes: sanctions_exposure NOT set: needs the venue's own Chainalysis/TRM screening of the team multisig (0xE6A4…2075), Emergency Council (0x9924…013D), foundation and top-holder addresses.

L04.rationale: Non-custodial AMM with no custody or issuance; Aero plans permissioned tiers for regulated institutions, which may raise licensing questions.

L05.rationale: No litigation or regulator action found in press or exchange disclosures; court and regulator databases were not searched directly.

L06.rationale: Plain ERC-20 and AMM contracts with no privacy or obfuscation features.

notes: missing: front-end geofencing and terms-of-use restrictions

gates.title: Unrestricted mint controlled by a single key
gates.why: Supply can be inflated at will; every other number in the report is conditional on one person's restraint.

gates.title: Sanctions / illicit-finance exposure
gates.why: Listing would create direct regulatory liability for the venue.

gates.title: Core contracts not source-verified
gates.why: Nobody outside the team can see what users are interacting with.

gates.title: Unremediated exploit with user losses
gates.why: Users are owed money; listing would expose new users to the same counterparty.

gates.title: Active enforcement action against the project or founders
gates.why: Outcome could force delisting or freeze assets after listing.

gates.title: Upgradeable contracts with no meaningful timelock
gates.why: Logic can change under users with no time to exit.

gates.title: Extreme holder concentration
gates.why: A handful of wallets can set the price; order books will not absorb their exit.

gates.title: Unlock cliff within 90 days
gates.why: More than a quarter of circulating supply unlocks shortly after a listing window.

gates.title: No independent audit
gates.why: Code holding user funds has never been reviewed by a third party.

gates.title: Material misrepresentation
gates.why: Two or more project claims contradicted by observed data — the reviewer cannot rely on anything self-reported.

gates.title: Security pillar failing
gates.why: Average security score below 1.5/4 — structural rather than one-off weakness.

gates.title: Anonymous team with centralised admin powers
Undisclosed market-maker terms
gates.why: Token loans and call options are where post-listing dumps are engineered.

gates.title: Insider-heavy allocation
gates.why: Team and investors hold more than half of supply.

gates.title: Mercenary TVL
gates.why: Most deposits are paid to be there and will leave when incentives stop.

gates.title: Volume implausible versus depth
gates.why: Daily volume more than 100x the ±2% depth is a common wash-trading signature.
